description: A consultation, check-up, or minor treatment that does not require the patient to be admitted to the hospital is generally not covered under PMJAY, which is built around secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
source_note: Reported government reply, Rajya Sabha (as cited in the source spec, Section 6.6). Carried forward from the spec's own research log (Section 22.1); not independently re-verified against the primary Rajya Sabha record during this build.

description: Cosmetic procedures — surgery intended to change appearance rather than treat a diagnosed medical or functional problem — are not covered under PMJAY. If a doctor has documented a genuine functional issue behind an otherwise cosmetic-sounding procedure, that changes how it may be classified; that judgement belongs to the treating doctor, not this tool.
source_note: Reported government reply, Rajya Sabha (as cited in the source spec, Section 6.6).

description: Fertility treatments, including IVF and related procedures, are not covered under PMJAY.
source_note: Reported government reply, Rajya Sabha (as cited in the source spec, Section 6.6).

description: Organ transplant is only partially covered, and only in some states, for specific procedures such as cornea or kidney transplant. Whether a specific transplant is covered genuinely depends on the state and the organ — this is not a simple yes or no, and should route to a human check rather than a confident answer either way.
nuance: State-dependent and procedure-specific. Route to amber (human-confirmation) rather than a flat red, since some transplant procedures genuinely are covered in some states.
source_note: Reported government reply, Rajya Sabha (as cited in the source spec, Section 6.6).
